newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK government paper yields rise on U.S. bond slump.
newsitem.headline: HK government paper yields rise on U.S. bond slump.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper yields rose across the board on Thursday on weaker U.S. bond prices dampened by better-than-expected U.S. economic data, dealers said.
"But the extent of the yields' rise is being capped by low trading volume," one European bank trader said.
Three-year notes yielded 6.13 percent versus 6.02 at Tuesday midday, the seven-year yield rose to 7.14 from 7.01 and the longest 10-year note yielded 7.41 versus 7.27 percent.
One-month bill yields also edged up at 4.34 percent versus 4.33 percent on Tuesday.

"The interest rate trend is still not very clear and U.S. treasuries probably should trade within a range until non-farm payroll and producer price index due later provide a better picture," a dealer at a U.S. bank said.
In the money market, short-term money remained liquid with overnight rate falling more than half a pecentage point this morning, after jumping on Tuesday on year-end demand, dealers said.
Overnight cash eased to 4-5/8 9/16 from 5-1/4 1/8 percent at midday on Tuesday and three-month money fell 1/16 to 5-1/2 3/8 percent. -- Alison Leung (852) 2843 6369
